# Guard Core MCP Documentation - LLMs.txt
# For LLM Crawlers and AI Assistants
# Documentation Site: https://rennf93.github.io/guard-core-mcp

## Overview
Guard Core MCP is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that lets AI coding agents answer questions about the Guard security ecosystem, fastapi-guard, guard-core and guard-agent, by introspecting the libraries actually installed in a project, instead of answering from training data. This documentation site covers installation, all six tools, and release notes.

## Documentation Structure

### Getting Started
- **Home**: https://rennf93.github.io/guard-core-mcp/latest/
- **Installation**: https://rennf93.github.io/guard-core-mcp/latest/installation/

### Tools Reference
- **All Six Tools**: https://rennf93.github.io/guard-core-mcp/latest/tools/
  - `versions`, which Guard libraries are installed, at what version, and what the bundled docs cover
  - `validate_config`, validate a config dict against the real `SecurityConfig`/`AgentConfig` model
  - `config_fields`, look up a config field by exact name or fuzzy query
  - `search_docs`, search the bundled fastapi-guard/guard-core/guard-agent documentation
  - `get_doc`, fetch the full text of one bundled documentation page
  - `check_payload`, run a request through guard-core's real detection engine

### Release Notes
- **Changelog**: https://rennf93.github.io/guard-core-mcp/latest/release-notes/

## Key Facts

### The Ecosystem
- **fastapi-guard**: Security middleware for FastAPI applications
- **guard-core**: Framework-agnostic security library that fastapi-guard builds on
- **guard-agent**: Telemetry and monitoring agent for the Guard security ecosystem

### Why This Server Exists
Pydantic silently ignores unknown config keys instead of raising, so a misspelled setting does nothing at runtime with no error anywhere. `guard-core-mcp` answers config and detection questions from the packages actually installed in the interpreter running it, real Pydantic validation, real field metadata, and the real guard-core detection engine, rather than from an LLM's memory of the library, which may be stale or wrong for the installed version.

### Installation Model
`guard-core-mcp` must run in the same environment as the Guard libraries it introspects:

```bash
uv add --dev guard-core-mcp
claude mcp add guard-core -- uv run guard-core-mcp
```

Running it via `uvx guard-core-mcp` is explicitly the wrong way to install this server: `uvx` builds an isolated environment containing only `guard-core-mcp`'s own dependencies (`mcp`, `pydantic`), so `validate_config`, `config_fields` and `check_payload` all degrade to a structured `{"error": ..., "hint": ...}` response, only `versions`, `search_docs` and `get_doc` still work, since the documentation ships bundled inside the wheel.

### Runtime Dependencies
Only `mcp` and `pydantic`, `fastapi-guard`, `guard-core` and `guard-agent` are never installed by `guard-core-mcp` itself. They must already be present in the environment it runs in.
